summary: High-frequency audit webhook: ordering guarantees, per-event idempotency, and sample redaction mapping for Splunk HEC
summary_long: Customer requests ordering and deduplication guarantees for a high-throughput audit webhook, plus a small sample of redacted payloads and a field-mapping file for Splunk HEC ingestion. They report out-of-order events and duplicate IDs causing downstream reconciliation gaps.
description: Issue summary: FinCloud Capital uses Redwood's live audit webhook to stream tenant-scoped activity into their Splunk HEC cluster. Over the last 72 hours they observed event sequences arriving out-of-order and occasional duplicate event_ids, causing their dedupe+windowing logic to drop legitimate transactions. They want: (1) a documented guarantee of ordering semantics (per-tenant watermark or monotonic sequence), (2) per-event idempotency token behavior and TTL, (3) a small redacted sample payload set mapped to Splunk HEC fields, and (4) guidance for resuming ingestion from a resume-token if a window gap occurs.
impact: Customer-facing: Splunk-based reconciliation reports show missing transactions for two accounts (revenue-impacting). FinCloud has paused daily reconciliation and classified this as P1 because it affects month-end reporting. Risk of regulatory reporting errors if unresolved.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer subscribes to live audit webhook for tenant T-78 using HMAC-authenticated delivery to their HTTPS endpoint.
2) Traffic profile: 1200 events/minute burst, typical sequence numbers assigned by Redwood per event.
3) Customer processes events with dedupe by event_id and time-window of 30s. They observe (a) event_id duplicates within <10s and (b) sequence numbers that jump backward by 1-3 for some windows.
4) Customer captures first_occurrence and last_received timestamps and provided them in attached logs.
5) When the customer retries delivery acknowledgement, some duplicates are reprocessed and others are dropped by their ingestion logic.
6) Customer requested sample redacted payloads and mapping table to validate field-level masking for PII-sensitive attributes.
customer_notes: We started seeing this after ramping from 200 to 1200 events/minute last Thursday; previously stable for 6 months.
We use per-tenant dedupe tables keyed by event_id and sequence; duplicates lead to dropped rows in downstream joins.
support_activity: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Aisha K (Support): Acknowledged and requested latest logs and webhook delivery trace. Assigned to platform-ingest team.
2026-03-10 11:03 UTC - Liam C (Platform Eng): Confirmed receipt of attachment and started ingest trace correlation. Opened INT-5321 to collect broker delivery metrics.
2026-03-11 02:40 UTC - SRE (internal): Noted transient producer backfill retry bursts from queue shard s-4 between 2026-03-08T14:00-14:06Z. Created telemetry snapshot.
2026-03-12 17:55 UTC - Customer (FinCloud): Provided sample CSV of their dedupe rules and requested confirmation of idempotency token semantics.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: transient reordering caused by cross-shard retry and prefetch on delivery worker, combined with client-side processing assumptions about monotonic seq numbers.
Telemetry: broker delivery log shows duplicate handoffs for event_id evt-78-0001 with two different seq values; occurrence aligns with a consumer restart and immediate producer retries.

Ingest runtime: sequence numbers are assigned at generation time per-tenant, but ordering guarantees are best-effort per shard. When an event is retried from dead-letter or retry queue it can be re-emitted with the original seq but may arrive after later seqs if cross-shard routing happened.
Auth/HMAC: no evidence of replay attack; HMAC timestamps valid and within TTL.
mitigation_steps_taken: Added short-term guidance to customer to widen dedupe window to 60s and accept idempotency by event_id instead of strict seq monotonicity.
Enabled per-tenant sticky routing to preferred shard for T-78 for 24 hours to reduce cross-shard retries during peak bursts.
Queued a platform change proposal to emit a resume_token with per-batch high-watermark for ordered delivery. See PR referenced above.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Increased routing stickiness and recommended dedupe window change. Long-term plan: implement explicit per-batch resume_token + optional monotonic offset header and document idempotency semantics in the webhook API docs. Customer accepted workaround and scheduled a follow-up validation run on 2026-03-14. Escalated to Product for API doc update.

public_response_snippet: Thanks for the report — we've isolated a retry/reorder pattern under burst conditions and applied a temporary routing fix. We'll provide updated docs and a resume-token API field to give deterministic resume/reconciliation. Working with you on a validation window on 03/14.
security_considerations: No evidence of credential compromise. Payload redaction confirmed in attached sample. Product will update docs to call out PII redaction fields and recommended minimal surface for Splunk HEC mapping.
